title: Main store of the first stored-program machines, in binary digits
description: Bar chart on a logarithmic scale of each machine's main (random-access or delay-line) store in binary digits. Manchester Baby, 1948: 32 words of 32 bits, 1,024. EDSAC, 1949: 512 words of 17 bits, 8,704. Ferranti Mark 1, 1951: 8 pages of 64 lines of 20 bits, 10,240. UNIVAC I, 1951: 1,000 words of 12 six-bit characters, 72,000, not counting check pulses. IBM 701, 1952: 2,048 words of 36 bits, 73,728. Data: University of Manchester, University of Cambridge Computer Laboratory, Weik 1955.
heading: MAIN STORE · BINARY DIGITS (LOG SCALE)
